title: Tinsley Hill (15Ly18): Mississippian Town in Lyon County
summary: Tinsley Hill (15Ly18), in Lyon County, is a late prehistoric stone-grave cemetery and village studied in a federal salvage archaeology program.
bodyMarkdown:
Tinsley Hill (15Ly18) is a late prehistoric town and cemetery in Lyon County. The people who lived there belonged to the [Mississippian](https://grokipedia.com/page/Mississippian_culture) world, the farming chiefdoms that spread across the Southeast and the Ohio and Mississippi valleys between about 900 and 1500 AD. They grew corn, beans, and squash, built houses of poles and clay, and buried many of their dead in graves lined with stone slabs.

The site is known mostly from work done in a hurry. In the years after World War II, the federal government ran the Inter-Agency Archaeological Salvage Program. Its job was to study and record sites before new federal dams and reservoirs covered them. Tinsley Hill was one of those sites. Archaeologist Douglas W. Schwartz wrote a University of Kentucky report on the stone-grave cemetery, and R. Berle Clay led a separate dig on the village in 1962.

Stone-box graves are one of the clearest marks of Mississippian life in western Kentucky and middle Tennessee. Each grave was a small chamber built from flat stones set on edge, with a stone lid laid over the top. Grave goods, when found, can tell archaeologists about trade, rank, and belief.

The catalog records for the two reports are short. They place the work in Lyon County but do not give a mound count, a burial count, or a firm date range, so this story leaves those out rather than guess.

Tinsley Hill belongs with other Mississippian places in the western end of the state, such as [Wickliffe Mounds](/stories/wickliffe-mounds-mississippian-village-ballard-county/), the [Tolu site](/stories/tolu-site-mississippian-mounds/), and the [Jonathan Creek center](/stories/jonathan-creek-mississippian-center/). Together they show that western Kentucky held busy, organized towns centuries before European contact.

## Kentucky today

Tinsley Hill is not open to visitors, and its exact location is not published, to protect it from looting. The map pin is a rounded Lyon County point. Digging into or collecting from a Native grave is a crime under Kentucky law. The best place to see Mississippian life up close is Wickliffe Mounds State Historic Site in Ballard County.
Source: [Tinsley Hill Site: A Late Prehistoric Stone Grave Cemetery in Lyon County, Kentucky (tDAR)](https://core.tdar.org/document/176640/tinsley-hill-site-a-late-prehistoric-stone-grave-cemetery-in-lyon-county-kentucky)
Source: [Tinsley Hill Village, 1962 (tDAR)](https://core.tdar.org/document/176642/tinsley-hill-village-1962-a-project-of-the-inter-agency-archaeological-and-paleontological-salvage-program)
